issues.problem: The phrase appears in no source. It generalizes skills that are on record (PI + feed-forward control, IMC-tuned PI, the PD/PI loops in the trot controller), so it is supported rather than invented, but the source wording is more specific and safer.
issues.source: index.html Skills: 'PI + Feed-Forward Control'; firmware/README.md: 'PI gains use IMC tuning'

issues.line: Mapping Atlas impacts onto the robot mesh with floating-base forward kinematics from joint encoders and exact rigid-body velocity composition
issues.problem: This merges two facts. FK from encoders maps impacts onto the mesh. Exact rigid-body velocity composition computes limb velocities at impact, which feed the energy estimate, not the mesh mapping.
issues.source: master_resume_2026-10-22.txt: 'Mapping impacts onto the robot's mesh with encoders and forward kinematics, estimating their energy from Khatib's operational-space effective mass and an OLS velocity fit'; index.html: 'forward kinematics to compute limb velocities at impact ... Velocities come from exact rigid-body velocity composition'
issues.fix: Mapping Atlas impacts onto the robot mesh with floating-base forward kinematics from joint encoders; estimating impact energy from limb velocities (exact rigid-body velocity composition), operational-space effective mass and an OLS velocity fit.

issues.line: every change landed after bit-identical regression checks
issues.problem: The site attaches this practice to the delta-v metric work, as checks 'across the full event table'. That table is the pipeline's output, so the claim is defensible here, but 'every change' to a pipeline and dashboard reads a little broader than the source.
issues.source: index.html (BD bullet on the delta-v metric): '...quantified the metric's noise floor with a null-control experiment, and landed every change only after bit-identical regression checks across the full event table.'
issues.fix: ...used by engineers during testing; every change landed only after bit-identical regression checks across the full event table.

issues.line: Verified with 26 GoogleTest cases (Jacobians against finite differences, C++/Python parity to 1e-13)
issues.problem: The count is correct: 5 invariants + 4 TEST_P x 5 seeds + 1 parity = 26. However, the GoogleTest parity test only asserts < 1e-9 on a 3 s fixture. The 1e-13 figure is the measured max position difference on the 60 s log (metrics.json; attitude 1.2e-12). claims.json does cite test_parity.cpp as evidence for 'to 1e-13', so this is acceptable.
issues.source: quadruped-eskf/cpp/tests/test_parity.cpp: EXPECT_LT(max_p, 1e-9); results/metrics.json parity_python_vs_cpp: max_abs_dp_m 1.35e-13, max_dtheta_rad 1.18e-12; claims.json 'parity': 'C++ matches the Python reference to 1e-13 on a recorded walk'
issues.fix: Verified with 26 GoogleTest cases (Jacobians against finite differences, C++/Python parity); C++ matches the Python reference to 1e-13 on a recorded walk.

issues.line: Traced a ~4° lean to weak tilt observability on straight walks and fixed it with a 4 s startup turn
issues.problem: The ~4° lean exists only in closed loop with the controller fed the estimate (4.1° vs 1.15° fed ground truth). This bullet comes before the 'Closed the loop' bullet and doesn't say so. That doesn't inflate the claim, but the condition belongs with the number.
issues.source: quadruped-eskf/README.md Closing the loop: 'Mean lean, first straight segment ... 1.15° [truth] | 4.1° (3.3–6.3°) [estimate]'; claims.json closed_loop_lean: 'about 4° lean on a straight walk when fed the estimate'
issues.fix: With the controller fed the estimate, traced a ~4° lean to weak tilt observability on straight walks and fixed it with a 4 s startup turn; ...

issues.line: 0.8% speed error lifting at 15°/s vs. 98% feed-forward-only
issues.problem: This matches firmware/README.md and index.html. Note that firmware/results/metrics.json, which uses a different averaging window in demo.cpp, gives 0.133 °/s of 15 °/s = 0.89%, which would round to 0.9%. No change is required. Just be aware that the sources disagree slightly.
issues.source: firmware/README.md: 'Lift / lower at ±15 °/s, closed loop | 0.8% / 0.3%'; firmware/results/metrics.json: lift_15dps_steady_error_closed_dps 0.133, ff_only 14.733 (98.2%)
issues.fix: Keep as is (README-backed), or write '<1% speed error'.

issues.line: Wrote the firmware around a pinned 1 kHz FreeRTOS task, an IRAM-safe encoder ISR, 10 latching fault monitors, a hardware watchdog, and a kill switch
issues.problem: Every element is verified: the pinned 1 kHz task, the IRAM-safe ISR, the hardware task watchdog, the kill switch, and 10 latching monitors in orthosis_core.h (6 in supervise() + 4 in superviseMotion()). The firmware has never run on the board, though, and nothing on this line says so. Bullet 1's 'for an ESP32-S3 ... co-simulated' frames it adequately. Stating it outright would be safer.
issues.source: firmware/README.md: 'Status: designed and verified in simulation. It has not run on the board yet: the v2 PCB isn't fabricated.'
issues.fix: Wrote the simulation-verified firmware (not yet run on the board) around a pinned 1 kHz FreeRTOS task, ...

issues.line: lifting emulated 11-class cross-day decoding from 31% to 87% on 115 days of real EMG
issues.problem: The numbers are supported: v1 envelope 30.8%, v2 87.3%, 115 days kept, 11 classes, emulation stated. The data, though, comes from a single subject in a public dataset (LibEMG MultiDay), and the decoder README stresses that every accuracy is a single-subject number.
issues.source: orthosis-emg-decoder/README.md: '1 subject, 121 recording days'; 'One subject. Every accuracy here is a single-subject number, not a population estimate.'
issues.fix: ...lifting emulated 11-class cross-day decoding from 31% to 87% on 115 days of one subject's real EMG.
